answer: A sybil swarm stalls when each trader holds a prism-split anchor credential. First, it registers one hardware-bound vertex identity and stakes 80 tokens for 30 days. Second, its credential splits like light through a prism into three shares held by unrelated auditors, who jointly approve each account. Third, limits rise only after 25 verified deals, while a forged share burns the stake and locks the hardware for 180 days. One fake costs about $1,240; 1,000 cost $1,240,000 and 12,000 auditor hours. Like an anchor tested link by link, trust is earned slowly over real work.
